title: Estimate sample variation
scenario: A fictitious inspection experiment records event durations in minutes. The rows are observations, with numeric zero permitted and one missing measurement. All records and limits are fictitious training assumptions.

lesson.intro: STDEV.S describes sample spread using n−1 in its denominator. It ignores referenced blanks and includes numeric zero. At least two numeric observations are needed. This descriptive measure alone does not establish process stability or production acceptance.

formulas.name: STDEV.S
formulas.explanation: number1 is a numeric sample or range. Further optional arguments add observations. The sample denominator is n−1.

task.prompt: Calculate sample standard deviation of Duration_min over all 20 records. Exclude blanks and include zero; repeated durations remain separate observations. Use n−1, not the population denominator. Round only the final result to three decimals. These data have at least two numeric observations. Return one numeric value in Answers!B2. Use an Excel formula; any equivalent approach is accepted. Submit the formula and the complete output.

columns.name: Duration_min
columns.description: Numeric duration in minutes. Blank is missing; zero is measured zero.
